faqs.question: What does AFB (TB) – Antibiogram for MTb Complex – Amikacin Drug by MGIT – Pure Growth of MTB Complex measure?
faqs.answer: This test determines the susceptibility of the MTb complex to the drug amikacin.

faqs.question: Why is AFB (TB) – Antibiogram for MTb Complex – Amikacin Drug by MGIT – Pure Growth of MTB Complex done?
faqs.answer: • This test is primarily done to determine the drug susceptibility of MTb complex to amikacin. • Selecting appropriate medications for treating TB • Assessing the effectiveness of specific antibiotics • Preventing the development of drug resistance • Optimising treatment outcomes

faqs.question: When is AFB (TB) – Antibiogram for MTb Complex – Amikacin Drug by MGIT – Pure Growth of MTB Complex recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • When a patient is diagnosed with TB and requires guidance on which medications to use. • When TB treatment is not yielding the desired results. • When a patient has a history of contact with someone infected with drug-resistant TB. • When a patient's clinical condition worsens despite receiving TB treatment.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB (TB) – Antibiogram for MTb Complex – Amikacin Drug by MGIT – Pure Growth of MTB Complex are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may suggest resistance to amikacin, which means alternative drugs need to be considered for treating TB.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB (TB) – Antibiogram for MTb Complex – Amikacin Drug by MGIT – Pure Growth of MTB Complex?
faqs.answer: • Discuss any medications you are taking with your doctor, as some may interfere with the test results. • Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria. It primarily affects the lungs, but can also impact other organs. TB spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Symptoms include persistent cough, weight loss, fever, and fatigue. Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial to prevent complications and transmission.
